clue.text: Where graphic forecasts are found for Top of the Pops

definitions.meaning: weather forecasts are drawn as maps and diagrams, so they appear among the meteorological charts
the BBC's long-running pop music show featured records currently ranked in the best-seller list

explanation.surface: A quiz question about where weather maps belong, oddly linked to a TV pop show.
explanation.walkthrough: Top of the Pops was a weekly BBC television show playing the week's best-selling records.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather forecasts are printed as charts, and a hit record is listed among the week's best-sellers.

clue.text: Dowdiness is out of the question

definitions.text: Dowdiness is out of the question

parts.words: Dowdiness is out of the question
parts.note: being dowdy means not being 'on', the slang word for fashionable or in style, and the same phrase means unacceptable

explanation.surface: A fashion editor declares that frumpy clothes are simply unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unacceptable is said to be impermissible in colloquial speech, and the dowdy are not fashionable, so one phrase serves both.

clue.text: He had to upset the applecart!

definitions.text: He had to upset the applecart!

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over and disorder, so the letters of the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone impetuous was bound to spoil everybody's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HE HAD TO; the whole clue describes an impetuous person who wrecks plans, which is what 'upset the applecart' means.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash, impetuous person is exactly the sort who spoils carefully laid plans.

clue.text: May the monkey have a bite to eat?

parts.note: may in the sense of being permitted, as can is used colloquially
an ape is a primate, loosely a monkey

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the zoo monkey is allowed a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A small savoury on bread or pastry served at parties is a little snack.

clue.text: Bill has a living-that's the truth

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
a living is a church benefice, as is a curate's post

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that the bill comes with a comfortable income, honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'living' is the old term for a paid church post held by a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Correctness or exactness is close to truthfulness in a statement.

clue.text: Drag around Virginia to find work

indicators.note: around places the first piece encircling the state abbreviation

parts.note: to drag something along the ground is to trail it
VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A tired worker hauls their load around the state of Virginia to find a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, painful labour or toil is an old synonym for effort.

clue.text: Double profits time after time

explanation.surface: An investor brags about doubling returns repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeatedly happening is the same as over and over, and two profits are one gain and another gain.

clue.text: Raising financial support to the family occasions bitter criticism

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help such as money given
a tribe is a clan or extended family

explanation.surface: Asking relatives for money leads to angry words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long bitter verbal attack.

clue.text: Section report set out the historicalviewpoint

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A section of a report sets out the historical perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'historical' and 'viewpoint' together; read them as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking back over past events is a backward-looking view of history.

clue.text: Saw the point of telling a bird to vamoose

parts.note: vamoose is slang for leave, so telling someone to vamoose is saying go
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone understood why you'd shoo a bird away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telling a bird to vamoose' is the order 'Go, tit!'
explanation.definitionFit: Understood the joke or idea is a colloquial phrase for grasping it.

clue.text: Fruit drink fit for the gods in the East

parts.note: nectar was the drink of the Greek gods
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An exotic fruit juice is described as heavenly, from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is a stone fruit.

clue.text: Law-school custodian is a local man

parts.note: the Inns of Court are London's legal societies where barristers train
a keeper looks after something

explanation.surface: A guardian at a law college is a man from the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British slang for one's regular pub, so a 'local man' runs a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub landlord runs the neighbourhood bar, the British 'local'.

clue.text: Upin a prison

parts.note: stir is slang for jail

explanation.surface: Someone is detained in a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'Up' and 'in' together: read 'Up' as the definition and 'in' as a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Awake and moving about, out of bed.

clue.text: Like to absorb TGWU secretary in argument

indicators.note: absorb means take in, so the first word wraps round the union leader

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
Ron Todd was general secretary of the Transport and General Workers' Union

explanation.surface: A union leader is drawn into a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The TGWU was a big British trade union; Ron Todd led it in the late 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreeing or quarrelling, set against each other.

clue.text: Supreme Commander of the Normandy invasion

definitions.meaning: a ruler with power over others, a supreme lord
Operation ... was the 1944 Allied landing in France

explanation.surface: A title for Eisenhower, who led the D-Day landings.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal superior lord rules others, and the codename for the D-Day operation was the same word.

clue.text: Idiots say they're under Cornish administration

indicators.note: say tells us to listen to the word for fools as it is spoken

parts.note: sillies are foolish people

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that only fools let Cornwall run them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isles of Scilly lie off Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isles of Scilly, off the Cornish coast, are administered together with Cornwall.

clue.text: Priest in order which is unsullied

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new order rearranges the two words before

explanation.surface: A priest belongs to a religious order that keeps itself pure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a religious order beside 'Priest', but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless, in perfect original condition, untouched by dirt.

clue.text: People in charge of wardrobes and cupboards

definitions.meaning: theatre staff who look after actors' costumes and help them change
kitchen sideboards with shelves for crockery

explanation.surface: A list of furniture and the people who run costume rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre costume assistants and kitchen sideboards with shelves share one name.

clue.text: Throw on a cape kept in re serve

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A cloak thrown on is kept in the wardrobe for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticence or timidity is a quiet holding back.

clue.text: Current way to acknowledge paternity in Franglais

definitions.meaning: the unit of electric current, by metonymy

definitions.text: way to acknowledge paternity in Franglais
definitions.meaning: mixing English and French, a man would say he is the father, using the French word for father

explanation.surface: A modern way to admit fatherhood in mixed English and French.
explanation.walkthrough: Franglais is a jokey mix of French and English; père is French for father.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit measuring electric flow stands here for the flow itself.

clue.text: Compelled Irish terrorists to produce wine

parts.note: made someone do it means forced them
the IRA, the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: Paramilitaries are forced to make wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from the Portuguese Atlantic island.

clue.text: Give up again and withdraw

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to cede is to surrender or hand over

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders a second time and retreats.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull back or retreat, as floodwaters do.

clue.text: Goodness me, what a doll!

definitions.meaning: a golliwog, a black rag doll once common in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in delight at a pretty toy.
explanation.walkthrough: The doll sense is the golliwog, a rag doll now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild oath of surprise shares a name with a short form for an old rag doll.

clue.text: True, dates should be processed quickly

indicators.note: processing works the letters of the word before into a new form

parts.note: fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A food packer insists the dates must be dealt with promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be processed' rearranges DATES into STEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal and firm, unwavering in allegiance.

clue.text: Stagger from a labyrinth

parts.note: a maze is a labyrinth

explanation.surface: Someone staggers out of a labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish or astound someone is to stagger them.

clue.text: Disturbing realities for a descendant of Jacob

indicators.note: disturbing means unsettling, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unsettling facts about one of Jacob's line.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob was renamed Israel, so his descendants are the children of Israel.

clue.text: The state of some Florida holiday-makers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking about the home state of certain tourists in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the north-west Rockies.

clue.text: Silly woman scolded and swore

parts.note: a silly is a fool, as is an ass
Eve, the first woman
to rate is an old word for to scold

explanation.surface: A foolish woman was told off and cursed.
explanation.definitionFit: Declared solemnly or affirmed, as in swearing an oath.
